answer: An attacker who floods the jury with fake votes also floods itself with the cost of its own dishonest votes, because every vote is penalized when it backs a bad answer. This is why the network can stay open without a central gatekeeper: the economics of reputation do the filtering that a trusted authority otherwise would.. This matters because the cost of running many aliases grows faster than the influence they can exert, making the attack economically self-defeating. Consider a lantern as the anchor of the cost. A whisper stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a nadir hold...
